title: Learner 01 | Day 175: Individual mastery and repair: Python, API, SQL, and coding interviews
body:
## Goal

Individual mastery and repair: Python, API, SQL, and coding interviews

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/specializations/learner_01/core/capability.py`

**Method/unit:** `apply_capability`

**Why here:** This is inside your owned AI/ML capability and the named layer. Model/data SDK details stay in adapters, rules in core, and commands/results in experience. It plugs into the same shared project architecture as other capabilities.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Both solve fresh variants, explain complexity and failure behavior, and make a correct project change with focused feedback.

**Boundaries:** Keep the change inside the owned capability and preserve accepted behavior.

## Research hints

1. Research **one observed gap in Python output prediction and debugging / Backend system-design mock and remediation**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:docs.python.org one observed gap in Python output prediction and debugging Backend system-design mock`; use [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** Your partner reports a failure in capstone polish, maintainability, and demonstration. Using this week's concrete cases, how do you locate the first broken boundary, repair it, and explain the design choice?

**Review with @GlidingScorpion:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
